# Tako

> Tako is a data intelligence platform. The Tako MCP server lets AI agents search a proprietary, continuously-updated knowledge base of 100K+ curated charts — carrying the latest reported quarter, same-day market prices, and official releases as they publish, not static historical reference — get grounded answers, explore Tako's data graph, fetch underlying source content, and run a multi-step Answer Agent. It is a hosted remote MCP server on Cloudflare Workers.

## Documentation

- [MCP Server Setup](https://github.com/TakoData/tako-mcp): Connect to the hosted Tako MCP server
- [API Reference](https://tako.com/docs/): Full REST API documentation
- [Chart Gallery](https://tako.com/gallery): Browse example charts and visualizations
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://tako.com/openapi.yaml): Machine-readable API specification

## Connecting

Hosted endpoint: `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP).

- No credentials needed to start: an anonymous connection gets the free tier — `tako_search`, `tako_answer`, and `tako_available_data`, limited to 10 requests/min per IP. (ChatGPT additionally lists `tako_contents` and `tako_visualize` anonymously; they answer with a sign-in challenge until the account is linked.) Authenticating unlocks the full toolset and your own account limits.
- Config-file hosts (Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, or Claude Code via `claude mcp add`): pass `Authorization: Bearer <TAKO_API_TOKEN>`. Get a token at tako.com -> account settings -> API tokens.
- OAuth hosts (Claude Code plugin, Claude.ai, ChatGPT): connect via the server's OAuth flow; no token config needed.

Optional tools: some tools are opt-in and off by default, to keep the default surface small. Enable them by adding `?tools=` to the endpoint URL with comma-separated aliases, e.g. `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp?tools=agent,visualize`. Aliases: `agent` (Answer Agent — the server picks the single-call `tako_agent` on most clients and the `tako_agent_start` / `tako_agent_wait` pair on ChatGPT), `visualize` (`tako_visualize`; already on by default for ChatGPT and Claude, the hosts that render its chart widget inline), `credits` (`get_credit_balance`), `graph` (the low-level graph primitives `tako_graph_search` / `tako_graph_related` / `tako_graph_node` — power-user traversal beyond what `tako_available_data` covers). Only aliases are recognized (not raw tool names); unknown `?tools=` values are ignored, so a typo never breaks the connection.

Tools are discovered at runtime via `tools/list`. There is no per-call `api_token` argument — auth is connection-level.

## Available Tools

### Search vs. Answer — the core distinction

`tako_search` and `tako_answer` both read Tako's data graph and the live web, but return opposite things:

- **Want the DATA** — cards, rows, or a chart to work with or show? Use `tako_search`. It is fast and built to fan out: fire many narrow one-entity+one-metric queries in parallel and assemble the result yourself. The top card auto-renders inline as a chart.
- **Want one written ANSWER** to a single, specific data question? Use `tako_answer`. It returns one synthesized answer grounded in the cards it cites.

Never send a broad or multi-part question to either tool as one call — split it into narrow entity+metric searches (e.g. "US CPI inflation", "US core CPI inflation", "US PCE inflation", "US core PCE inflation"). In one line: `tako_search` hands you the evidence, `tako_answer` hands you the conclusion. For open-ended, multi-step research use `tako_agent` (opt-in).

### tako_search
Reconnaissance and chart retrieval across Tako's data graph and the live web, returned as structured `cards` plus `web_results`; the top card auto-renders inline as a chart (interactive widget on ChatGPT, chart image on other hosts). It locates data rather than delivering it: a card's rows are often license-gated and a web result is a snippet, so use it for breadth (many narrow queries fanned out in parallel to see what exists), for a chart when the embed is the deliverable, and to harvest node ids and urls. For a value or figure, ask `tako_answer` instead.

Built to fan out: each query should resolve one entity + one metric ("Apple revenue", "Nvidia vs AMD gross margin"), and many narrow queries fired in parallel retrieve far better than one broad or compound query. To see what proprietary data exists — or confirm a specific figure exists before you spend a query — check `tako_available_data` first (free). Ground a query by pinning resolved graph ids. For a card's full rows call `tako_contents` — only when the card is marked `exportable: true`. A non-exportable card (`exportable: false`, usually license-gated) carries no rows: read its headline value from the card's `description` when it carries one, or get specific figures via `tako_answer`, pinning that card's METRIC node id ALONE (the `mt::` entry in its `nodes`) with `strict: true` (each such card carries a `values_hint` saying exactly this). Repeated source/methodology paragraphs are hoisted out of the cards into the trailing Source Notes section of the markdown, keyed by source name — look a card's `source_name` up there (truncating clients lose boilerplate before data). For one written answer use `tako_answer`; for open-ended research use `tako_agent` (opt-in). Results arrive as a markdown document — a Tako Data section (per card: headline, exportable flag, node ids, chart link, a rows-count pointer), then Web Results, then Source Notes; the cards' actual rows and the web results' snippets ride in structuredContent (`cards[].content`, `web_results[].snippet`), not the markdown, alongside machine essentials (request_id, usage, chart-widget fields).

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): Natural-language query — one entity + one metric; parallelize multiple.
- `sources` (array): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for live web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `effort` (string, "fast" | "instant"): "fast" (default) or "instant" (fastest, cached embeds). Omit for fast.
- `count` (integer, 1-20, default 10): Maximum results per source.
- `include_contents` (boolean, default true): Inline each card's row preview; set false for a pointers-only response (cheaper when fanning out many parallel queries, or when coverage is unconfirmed). Full rows are always a separate `tako_contents` call.
- `preview_rows` (integer, 1-250, default 20): Cap on each card's inlined MOST-RECENT rows when `include_contents` is true. 20 is the free inline allowance the server ships — values above your account's allowance have no effect; lower it to trim context. For more rows call `tako_contents` (first 20 free, priced beyond). Ignored when `include_contents` is false.
- `country_code` (string, default "US"): ISO country code.
- `locale` (string, default "en-US"): Locale.
- `node_ids` (array of strings, max 20, optional): Graph node ids (from `tako_available_data`, or a card's `nodes`) to PIN into the proprietary data source — strong retrieval boost.
- `strict` (boolean, default false): Hard filter — when true, return ONLY cards matching at least one pinned node (requires non-empty `node_ids`).

### tako_answer
START HERE for any question seeking a value, figure, or finding: ask one specific, self-contained data question and get one synthesized answer grounded in the `cards` it cites. It is the only tool whose single response can finish the job — it reads cited pages internally, inlines cited cards' rows, auto-renders the top cited card inline as a chart, and returns a coverage verdict — where retrieval hands back captions and links you must then chase. The `answer` is already synthesized from its citations, and cited data cards carry a rows-count pointer in the prose, with the rows themselves in `structuredContent` (`cards[].content`), so the values arrive with the answer without being billed twice. When zero data cards ground the answer, a `guidance` field states the coverage miss deterministically (pivot; don't rephrase-retry). Also the values channel for non-exportable cards: when a search card is `exportable: false` (usually license-gated), ask here with that card's METRIC node id ALONE (the `mt::` entry in its `nodes`) pinned and `strict: true` to get the figures — pinning every node id on the card, or omitting strict, does not steer retrieval. Like `tako_search`, shared source/methodology paragraphs ride once in the trailing Source Notes section keyed by source name instead of repeating per card. For breadth or a chart card instead of a figure, use `tako_search` (parallelized into narrow entity+metric queries); when the question is what Tako covers, use `tako_available_data`. To pull a cited card's full rows, call `tako_contents` on its url (only when it's marked `exportable: true`). Results arrive as markdown — the synthesized answer first, then cited data cards (with a rows-count pointer, not the rows) and web citations, then Source Notes; the cited cards' actual rows ride in structuredContent (`cards[].content`), not the markdown, alongside machine essentials (request_id, usage, guidance).

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): One specific, self-contained question.
- `sources` (array, optional): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for live web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `include_contents` (boolean, default true): Inline each cited data card's recent rows alongside the answer; set false for prose + citations only (broad fan-outs, unconfirmed coverage). Cited web pages are never auto-inlined.
- `preview_rows` (integer, 1-250, default 20): Cap on each cited card's inlined MOST-RECENT rows when `include_contents` is true (20 = the free inline allowance the server ships; higher values have no effect). Ignored when it is false.
- `country_code` (string, default "US"): ISO country code.
- `locale` (string, default "en-US"): Locale.
- `node_ids` (array of strings, max 20, optional): Graph node ids to PIN into the proprietary data source — strong retrieval boost.
- `strict` (boolean, default false): Hard filter — when true, return ONLY cards matching at least one pinned node (requires non-empty `node_ids`).

### tako_contents
Fetch the real content behind result URLs (1-10 per call) from `tako_search` / `tako_answer` — the rows behind a Tako card (CSV by default, or JSON), or a web page's full text. It is the step after search when you need the full data to compute over or quote; a search result carries only a preview and a chart, not its rows. Batch them: fetching 8 pages in one call costs the same as 8 calls but saves 7 round trips, and every extra round trip re-sends the whole conversation as input tokens.

Precondition (Tako cards): non-exportable cards (`exportable: false`, usually license-gated) always 403 — never call this on them; their headline value is in the card's `description` (when present) and specific figures come from `tako_answer` (see the card's `values_hint`). Call only on `exportable: true` cards, and even then a rare card still 403s: fall back, don't retry. Web URLs always work.

Parameters:
- `urls` (array of string, 1-10, required): The result URLs to fetch — Tako card `webpage_url`s, web-result URLs, or a mix. Each is fetched and BILLED independently and one URL failing does not fail the others (its entry carries an `error` instead of a payload). Results are returned in `results`, positionally aligned with the URLs you passed.
- `url` (string, optional): Deprecated single-URL form, equivalent to `urls: [url]`. Prefer `urls`.
- `content_format` (string, optional): Tako cards only — serialization of the data: `csv` (default, text in `data`), `json_records` (row objects in `records`), or `json_compact` (compact columns+rows in `dataset`). Ignored for web URLs (always text).
- `max_rows` (integer, 1-2000, optional): Tako cards only — max rows to return. Omit for the free 20-row default; raise up to 2,000 for a larger (priced) export. Ignored for web URLs (use `max_chars`).
- `max_chars` (integer, 1-1,000,000, optional): Web URLs only — character cap on the extracted page text (1,000,000 = full text). Inline fetches default to 100,000; billing is per page regardless, so the cap only trims what reaches you (`truncated: true` reports a cut). Raise it toward 1,000,000 for a full long document inline. In url mode the downloaded file is the full text unless you set this (an explicit value caps the file too). Ignored when `query` is set (passages always scan the full text) and for Tako card URLs (use `max_rows`).
- `query` (string, optional): Web URLs + inline mode only — return just the passages around case-insensitive matches of this query (full phrase first, per-word fallback) instead of the full page text; one call lands on the relevant section of a long page, and the full text is always scanned regardless of `max_chars`. The `note` field summarizes the matches; a no-match note says so explicitly (a deterministic miss — try another url, not another wording). Ignored for Tako card URLs and in url mode.
- `mode` (string, "inline" | "url", default "inline"): Delivery only, not row count — `inline` returns the data in the response so you can read it; `url` returns a short-lived presigned `download_url` to the same file.

### tako_available_data
Find what proprietary, continuously-updated structured data exists on something — summarized in one call. Free and fast. Ask it when the question IS coverage: what does Tako have on X, is this measure tracked at all, what is it called — then build the real question around what comes back. NOT a required first step: for a straightforward data question, `tako_search` or `tako_answer` directly is usually right. Worth one call first when you need a measure's EXACT name, since resolving it to the canonical form measurably improves what the priced call retrieves. Works on an entity (a company, person, or place → the metrics tracked on it, e.g. Tesla) or a metric (→ the entities it is tracked across, e.g. Inflation Rate), reported as a natural-language summary you can show the user.

Two paths, chosen by whether you pass `metric`:
- **Lookup** (`q` + `metric`, e.g. `q="Carnival", metric="passenger cruise days"`) — resolves the entity+metric PAIR directly in ~0.6s and returns a runnable `next_call`. Use it whenever you already know the measure.
- **Discovery** (`q` alone) — lists what the resolved node covers, for browsing. Candidate names are relevance-gated against `q` (name matches rank above alias matches), so a fuzzy graph hit about a different company is not reported as coverage.

The exact metric/entity names are the terms to reuse in the follow-up call; `structuredContent.matches[].coverage.items[]` pairs each name with its `node_id`. To land on exactly one metric, pin THAT metric node id alone with `strict: true` and name the entity in the query text — an entity-only pin, or a pin without `strict`, is a measured no-op. When the measure is known, `next_call` is that follow-up prewritten (query + the metric node + `strict`) — run it verbatim.

A broad entity's coverage list is capped and may be truncated: treat a name you don't see as UNCONFIRMED rather than absent. This tool confirms a name EXISTS in the graph; it cannot confirm a chart exists behind it — the `next_call` is that check, and if it comes back with 0 cards, run the same query once more with `node_ids` removed before concluding Tako has no data: the pin is a hard filter and the data is often held under a sibling metric node. `found: false` is a real answer: report the gap rather than silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `q` (string, required, min 2 chars): The NAME of the entity (or metric) to look up. Put the measure in `metric`, not here.
- `metric` (string, optional, min 2 chars): The measure you want, when you already know it — e.g. "gross margin", "capex". Supplying it selects the fast lookup path above.
- `types` (string, "entity" | "metric", optional): Narrow resolution to a thing ("entity") or a measure ("metric"); omit to search both.
- `label` (string, optional): NER label to prefer — a boost, not a filter. Supply it when you can categorize the term (company→ORG, country→GPE, person→PERSON, metric→METRIC, …). Describes the ENTITY only; it is not applied to `metric`.

### tako_graph_search
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=graph` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Low-level primitive behind `tako_available_data` — prefer that tool for everyday coverage discovery. Resolve a name to Tako data-graph node ids with full control over the search: one kind per call — a thing (`types: "entity"`) or a measure (`types: "metric"`). Results are popularity-ordered; read each node's `subtype`/`label`/`description` to pick the right one. To explore a resolved node's connections, call `tako_graph_related` on its id.

Parameters:
- `q` (string, required): Search text (min 2 chars).
- `types` (string, "entity" | "metric", optional): Resolve a thing ("entity") or a measure ("metric"); omit to search both — but decide up front, don't mix the two in one call.
- `label` (string, optional): NER label to prefer — a boost, not a filter. Supply it when you can categorize the term (company→ORG, country→GPE, person→PERSON, metric→METRIC, …).
- `infer_label` (boolean, optional, default true): Auto-detect the label from `q`.
- `limit` (integer, 1-50, default 20): Max results.

### tako_graph_related
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=graph` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Explore what a resolved graph node connects to — the map of what data Tako has for it. Free. Covers what `tako_available_data` does not: traversal relations (siblings, part_of, members, `rel:*` named edges like `rel:competes_with`), server-side `q` filtering within a relation, and cursor paging past the first page. Drilling `relation: "metrics"` returns only that node's metrics group — the smallest, cheapest view of its coverage; the overview (`node_id` alone) also returns entities, siblings, and named edges at more tokens. A listed metric is table-level evidence, not proof — `tako_search` is the final validator. Empty `items` is a normal answer: report the gap instead of silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `node_id` (string, required): Node id from `tako_graph_search`, `tako_available_data`, or a card's `nodes`.
- `relation` (string, optional): Relation key to page — metrics, entities, siblings, part_of, members, or rel:<phrase>. Omit for the overview.
- `q` (string, optional): Case-insensitive substring filter on name+aliases — one string per call; for several name-variants of a metric ("revenue", "sales"), call once per variant.
- `label` (string, optional) / `infer_label` (boolean, optional): NER-label preference, as in `tako_graph_search`.
- `cursor` (string, optional) / `limit` (integer, 1-100, default 50): Pagination within a drilled relation.

### tako_graph_node
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=graph` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Get full detail for one graph-node `id` — name, aliases, subtype, label, description. Use it when you hold a bare node id (e.g. from a `tako_search` card's `nodes`, which carry only id/name/type) and need more to compose a grounded query or confirm what it is.

Parameters:
- `id` (string, required): Opaque public node id.

### tako_visualize
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=visualize` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Already on by default for ChatGPT and Claude, which render its chart inline as a widget; other clients enable it for the shareable embed URL. Create an embeddable Tako card from your OWN structured data (not from search), backed by Tako's Thin-Viz API. Provide one or more typed components; the card auto-renders inline as a chart and returns share/embed URLs.

Parameters:
- `components` (array, required): One or more `{ component_type, config, component_variant? }` objects. `component_type` is one of: header, generic_timeseries, categorical_bar, choropleth, data_table_chart, histogram, pie, table, financial_boxes, timeline, treemap, heatmap, marimekko, boxplot, waterfall, sankey, scatter, bubble, top_level_metric, person_card. `config` holds that type's data (validated server-side). The optional `component_variant` string selects a type variant (e.g. 'simple', 'financial'). `person_card` must be the only component.
- `title` (string, optional): Card title
- `description` (string, optional): Card description
- `source` (string, optional): Data source attribution shown in the footer
- `height` (integer, 100-2000, optional): Chart height in pixels
- `normalize_currencies` (string, optional): Target ISO 4217 code to convert currency-denominated datasets

### tako_agent
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=agent` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Run Tako's Answer Agent for open-ended, multi-step questions whose shape needs figuring out — cohorts, ranking or filtering by criteria, aggregation, and multi-hop reasoning across many entities; also the fallback when `tako_search` / `tako_answer` return nothing. Returns a synthesized answer plus supporting chart cards (~30–90s). On ChatGPT, exposed as the `tako_agent_start` / `tako_agent_wait` pair to fit the host's tool-call timeout model.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): The open-ended, analytical question.
- `sources` (array, optional): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for open-web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `thread_id` (string UUID, optional): Continue a prior agent run's thread as a follow-up; omit to start a new thread.

### get_credit_balance
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=credits` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Check the connected account's API credit balance.

Parameters: none.
